title: Sections of quasi-coherent algebras descend along smooth scheme covers
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $\mathcal Z$ be an algebraic stack over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}$-algebra, with big fppf site, precomposition restriction and global sections as in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Let $(p_i:U_i\to\mathcal Z)_{i\in I}$ be a small jointly surjective family of representable smooth morphisms from schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-size-convention]. Representable means representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]; smoothness is tested on their etale scheme charts. Joint surjectivity means that after every scheme base change these maps cover all points of the target. Write $R_{ij}=U_i\times_{\mathcal Z}U_j$, an algebraic space, with projections $r_1,r_2$, using [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Pullback gives a natural ring isomorphism $$\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\mathcal C)\ \cong\ \{(c_i)\in\prod_{i\in I}\Gamma(U_i,p_i^*\mathcal C):r_1^*c_i=r_2^*c_j\text{ in }\Gamma(R_{ij},\mathcal C|_{R_{ij}})\text{ for all }i,j\}.$$ Thus every compatible family descends uniquely, and equality of global sections can be checked on the $U_i$. Neither the $U_i$ nor the relation spaces are required affine or quasi-compact, and neither $\mathcal Z$ nor $\mathcal C$ is subject to a finiteness or Deligne--Mumford hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 076S (lemma-map-from-quasi-coherent), applied to the structure module and a quasi-coherent algebra, in the smooth presentation of Tag 06WV (lemma-quasi-coherent-algebraic-stack)(1). It identifies maps from the structure sheaf, hence sections, with the compatible chart maps. Apply to the disjoint-union smooth atlas; relation objects are algebraic spaces, not assumed schemes or affine. Ring operations are pointwise.

proof.text: Put $x_i=p_i\in\mathcal Z(U_i)$. With the precomposition restriction and global-section convention of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], a section on $U_i$ is an element of $\mathcal C(x_i)$: evaluate its compatible family at $\mathrm{id}_{U_i}$, and recover the family by restriction. A section on $R_{ij}$ is likewise a compatible family on all its scheme tests. In the $2$-fibre-product description [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], two arrows from an object $z\in\mathcal Z(W)$ to $x_i,x_j$ determine a map $W\to R_{ij}$, with the isomorphism between the two induced objects given by those arrows. The assumed equality on $R_{ij}$ therefore says that the two restrictions of $c_i,c_j$ to $\mathcal C(z)$ agree. This includes $i=j$ and different arrows to the same chart, so automorphisms are included in the compatibility condition.

proof.text: For each object $x\in\mathcal Z(T)$ form the algebraic spaces $P_i=T\times_{\mathcal Z}U_i$; these exist by representability in the hypotheses. Their projections to $T$ are smooth by [lem-sfb-stack-smooth-permanence], and jointly surjective by the hypothesis on $(p_i)$. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $W_i\to P_i$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The composite $W_i\to T$ is smooth because smoothness of the space map $P_i\to T$ means smoothness of its composites with representable etale scheme charts [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Since each $W_i\to P_i$ is surjective, the $W_i\to T$ are jointly surjective. It is flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Consequently $(W_i\to T)_i$ is an fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site]. Each chart supplies arrows $w_i\to x$ and $w_i\to x_i$, where $w_i\in\mathcal Z(W_i)$ is its induced object, with the specified $2$-isomorphism in the fibre product. Thus it is also a cover of $x$ in the big fppf site of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. All index sets and charts are in the stipulated size convention; no finite subcover is taken.

proof.text: Restrict each $c_i$ along $w_i\to x_i$, obtaining $a_i\in\mathcal C(w_i)$. On $W_i\times_TW_j$, the two induced arrows to $x_i,x_j$ have their specified common object over $x$; step 1 makes the restrictions of $a_i,a_j$ equal. The sheaf equalizer in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], applied to the underlying sheaf of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], gives a unique $s_x\in\mathcal C(x)$ restricting to these $a_i$. More generally the same construction applies to any fppf cover of $x$ equipped with arrows to the $x_i$. Two such covers give the same $s_x$: their pairwise fibre products over $T$ form a common covering refinement by the base-change and composition axioms of the site; on each refined member the restrictions are equal by step 1, and the injectivity part of the sheaf equalizer gives equality on $x$.

source.place: Tags 06TP (definition-inherited-topologies), 06TR (definition-sheaves); objectwise sheaf argument underlying Tag 076S (lemma-map-from-quasi-coherent). The assembly argument is written by Q58 from the definitions.

proof.text: For an arbitrary arrow $b:y\to x$ over $T'\to T$, pull the covering used for $x$ back to $T'$. It is a covering of $y$ by the base-change axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and its members retain their arrows to the same $x_i$. By functoriality of the restriction maps of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], $b^*s_x$ restricts there to the corresponding pullbacks of $c_i$. Step 3 and its independence of the chosen cover imply $b^*s_x=s_y$. Thus $(s_x)_x$ is a global section in precisely the compatible-family convention of that definition. When $x=x_i$, compare with the identity covering of $x_i$, equipped with its identity arrow to $x_i$; step 3 gives $s_{x_i}=c_i$. This proves existence of a global section inducing the prescribed family, including its invariance under all arrows over identity scheme maps.

source.place: Tags 06TP (definition-inherited-topologies), 06TR (definition-sheaves); objectwise sheaf argument underlying Tag 076S (lemma-map-from-quasi-coherent). The assembly argument is written by Q58 from the definitions.

proof.text: If two global sections restrict equally to all $U_i$, evaluate them at any object $x$ and then on the cover from step 2. Their values on each covering member equal the pullbacks of their values at $x_i$, hence agree. The injectivity in the sheaf equalizer [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] gives equality at $x$, so the global families are equal. Pullback preserves addition, multiplication and $1$ by [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]; hence the now bijective restriction map is a ring isomorphism onto the displayed compatible-family subring. Its naturality follows because it is restriction on every component, and a map commuting with this restriction commutes with its unique inverse. If $I$ is empty, joint surjectivity forces every scheme admitting an object of $\mathcal Z$ to be empty; the empty fppf cover then forces a unique section at every such object. The same argument therefore gives the one-element ring on both sides.
